properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/12/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/12/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 955503
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/12/2022
Comments: On May 12, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The area where the water was seeping out near the northwest stormwater vault observed on March 3, 2022 was not flowing. The small berm that was built to collect the seep was was dry and any water that is collected in that area is being vacuumed out. Upon arrival at the well pad, STL Resources was vacuuming water out of the northwest stormwater vault. The conductivity of the water that could not be vacuumed out was 2,500 uS/cm. About 18 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in this vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. STL Resources has back filled and rebuilt the excavated southwest and northwest infiltration berms that were impacted by the spill. DEP screened the water that had pooled up behind the northwest infiltration for conductivity and that resulted in 187 uS/cm. The conductivity of the small amount of water that pooled up behind the southwest infiltration berm was 40 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 22.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 23.1 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 188 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 196.2 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 59.9 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 44.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 133.4 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 25.2 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. During the inspection, STL Resources consultants were collecting soil samples from the well pad in a grid like pattern to delineate the area of the production fluid spill. Two of the holes that remained open had water pooled in them. Test Pit-209 which was about 7 yards to the north of the northwest stormwater vault had water pooled in it. The conductivity of the water in test pit-209 was 2030 uS/cm and soil conductivity was difficult to measure to due the looseness of the soil in the hole. Soil sample 0651-117 was collected from this test pit and will be analyzed for the Bureau of Labs SAC 530. Test Pit 211 which was about 15 yards to the north of 035-21325, had water pooled in it. The conductivity of the water was 3,800 uS/cm and the soil conductivity was 1,180 uS/cm. Soil Sample 0651-118 was collected from this test pit and will be analyzed for the Bureau of Labs SAC 530. DEP spoke with STL Resources Seth Rodriguez and he said that STL Resources is planning to hydroseed the site's earthen infiltration berms and parts of the site that are lacking vegetation. Infiltration berms 1, 2, 5, 6, and 8 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/27/2026 to APOLLO RESOURCES LLC in Snow Shoe Township, Centre county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: APOLLO RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/27/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8282218
Permit API: 027-21356
Unconventional: No
County: Centre
Municipality: Snow Shoe Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/27/2026
Comments: I conducted a site inspection on the morning of July 27, 2026 with the property owner. The inspection was concerning a brine release that was reported to the Department on July 25, 2026 by Jim Stiffler of Apollo Resources. According to Mr. Stiffler, the property owner was moving a trailer on the evening of July 24, 2026 and hit a 3" flange on the brine tank with the trailer, resulting in a brine release of 3,200 gallons of brine fluids.During the inspection I viewed the production equipment and the brine release area. Sandy, wet soils, and dead vegetation was observed in the brine release pathway. Approximately 6" of brine fluids still remain in the 100 BBL brine tank. Brine fluids traveled approximately 64' from the brine tank and approximately 30' wide. An old filled in pit from when the well was drilled is located in the pathway of the brine release. I screened multiple soil locations using a Hanna soil probe. Conductivity readings >4.00 mS/cm were observed.A stream (South Fork Beech Creek) is located downslope of the well site. I screened the stream both upstream and downstream of the brine release, readings were 48 uS/cm upstream and 52 uS/cm downstream.Due to the amount of brine fluid's released/reported, the Department recommends pursing Act 2 for site remediation. Violations have been cited.

Comments: Weather was 77° and sunny. Met with Chesapeake representative Kevin O'Sullivan. on location. Well recently had all casing strings set and cemented. Creston took sample where gas was detected. A 0 to 5k PSI analog pressure gauge was attached to the well head reading approximately 0 PSI. Well is scheduled to be completed in early September.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 4/21/2026
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone called made by Jeff Passarello, of Seneca Resources, to Alexis Jacobs, WQS with the Department, on April 20th, 2026. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred on the E08-T well pad.It was reported that approximately 1 barrel of production fluid was released from a maintenance failure on a pump used to support the transport of production fluid through a pipeline. The failure was immediately addressed and corrected to stop the production fluid from leaving the pipeline. The pump was in secondary containment, although a majority of the production fluid discharged outside of the containment onto the well pad and onto the fill material beyond the well pad. Upon arrival to the site, a skid steer was being used to remove contaminated material from the well pad. One dumpster was on site which contained the contaminated waste from the incident. A second dumpster was being transported to the site at the time of this inspection. The released production fluid appeared to be primarily within 10 yards of where the incident occurred on the well pad. Inspection Date: 3/25/2024
Comments: On 3/25/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at Seneca's Bieser Unit 833 well site in Chatham Township, Tioga County. It was 50 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by one infiltration basin on the north side of the pad.When I arrived on the well pad, I met Seneca's Brandy Davis who described current operations as follows. There were two unconventional wells on the site listed with the department as abandoned. Yost Drilling was on site with a workover rig, conducting plugging operations on each well. Brandy said that the Bieser 1V well had already been plugged and was in the process of being monitored for pressure for 45 days before the plugged well monument would be installed. The rig was set up on the Bieser 2H well. The crew had installed three plugs down hole and were preparing to trip in with the cutter. They were going to section mill from 2570 to 2590 feet and conduct a cement squeeze job at the milled section. The rig would then cement the upper section. Brandy accompanied me during site inspection. Secondary containment had been installed at the location prior to staging the work over rig. Work over operations were being conducted within the secondary containment structure. The mud pump and mud tank were stationed in the secondary containment structure along with the diesel tank. Two frac tanks were stationed in secondary containment west of the work over rig. Brandy said only fresh water was used in the tanks but that the wells had been circulated back to the tanks prior to plugging operations. Water/mud within the rig secondary containment structure field tested at 4.0 mS conductance. The Hanna Groline tester's upper limit is 4.0 mS conductance. There was water/mud puddles on the pad surface. A puddle northeast of the rig and outside of secondary containment field tested at 1.20 mS conductance. A 75'x12'x1" water puddle on unprotected ground on the northwest side of the rig field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. The upper limit for conductance with the Oakton PCTS5 is 19.99 mS. Sample #9551089 was collected from the water puddle northwest of the rig at Lat 41.864977, Long -77.372253. Other water puddles on the pad surface field tested at less than 1.0 mS conductance.The elevated conductance water puddle was adjacent to the west end of the north perimeter berm, reaching within 15 feet of the outfall at the northwest corner of the pad. Multiple readings along the length were 19.99 mS conductance and on the west end, the puddle field tested at 12.33 mS conductance. Water puddles witnessed in the rock lined channel coming off the pad field tested at 0.7 mS conductance. Water in the infiltration basin field tested at 0.7 mS conductance.After the inspection I did discuss the area of elevated conductance with Brandy and with Seneca's HSE coordinator, Wayne Fletcher. Brandy said a vac truck was in route. Wayne said the area would be scraped and the pad surface screened.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the unprotected pad surface is a violation of CSL 402(b). Additional violations may be cited based on the sample results.The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.The DEP recommends assessing the area of elevated conductance fluid at the northwest side of the pad; clean/report as necessary. I left the site at 1620 hrs.

Brandy accompanied me during site inspection. Secondary containment had been installed at the location prior to staging the work over rig. Work over operations were being conducted within the secondary containment structure. The mud pump and mud tank were stationed in the secondary containment structure along with the diesel tank. Two frac tanks were stationed in secondary containment west of the work over rig. Brandy said only fresh water was used in the tanks but that the wells had been circulated back to the tanks prior to plugging operations. Water/mud within the rig secondary containment structure field tested at 4.0 mS conductance. The Hanna Groline tester's upper limit is 4.0 mS conductance. There was water/mud puddles on the pad surface. A puddle northeast of the rig and outside of secondary containment field tested at 1.20 mS conductance. A 75'x12'x1" water puddle on unprotected ground on the northwest side of the rig field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. The upper limit for conductance with the Oakton PCTS5 is 19.99 mS. Sample #9551089 was collected from the water puddle northwest of the rig at Lat 41.864977, Long -77.372253. Other water puddles on the pad surface field tested at less than 1.0 mS conductance.The elevated conductance water puddle was adjacent to the west end of the north perimeter berm, reaching within 15 feet of the outfall at the northwest corner of the pad. Multiple readings along the length were 19.99 mS conductance and on the west end, the puddle field tested at 12.33 mS conductance. Water puddles witnessed in the rock lined channel coming off the pad field tested at 0.7 mS conductance. Water in the infiltration basin field tested at 0.7 mS conductance.After the inspection I did discuss the area of elevated conductance with Brandy and with Seneca's HSE coordinator, Wayne Fletcher. Brandy said a vac truck was in route. Wayne said the area would be scraped and the pad surface screened.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the unprotected pad surface is a violation of CSL 402(b). Additional violations may be cited based on the sample results.The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.The DEP recommends assessing the area of elevated conductance fluid at the northwest side of the pad; clean/report as necessary. I left the site at 1620 hrs.

Comments: On 03/10/2026, an incident inspection was conducted at the Burnsworth 1-6H Well Site following receipt of a spill report submitted on 03/09/2026 (CTS 395657). I was accompanied by Laura Grada and Ralph Bard (PA DEP).The spill report indicated that a Chemical tote tipped over and released about 25 gallons of defoamer onto well pad gravel. Groundwater/storm drains dont seem to be impacted. SPSI in Washington en route for remediation, absorbent pads have been applied to spill area. Not sure when spill occurred, caller assumed sometime during the storm Saturday evening. It was noted that the spill occurred on 03/07/2026, or sometime over the weekend.I called Range Resources representative Nate Smiell on 03/10/2026 for information about the spill. It was noted that the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) was put on site, the spill was fully remediated, and the container was placed onto secondary containment. The operator submitted a photo of where the spill originated within the tan container (Photo 17). It was also shared that a summary email was being submitted for the spill.On 03/10/2026, at 12:27 pm, the operator submitted information regarding the spill that was reported to the Department on 03/09/2026: "As reported to the PADEP hotline at 1:55 PM on 3/9/2026.Burnsworth S and T Unit 10H (37-125-28884)93 Penn Hill RoadAmity, PA 15311Amwell Township, Washington CountyOn 3/9/2026 at 12:42 PM, while conducting a site check, a lease operator identified a chemical injection tote on its side. It appears that recent high winds blew the unit over and a portion of the contents were released from the fill cap vent. An estimated 25 gallons of defoamer released and was contained to the graveled well pad. Specialized Professional Services Inc. (SPSI) responded to the location and remediated the impacted areas placing the material into roll-off boxes for disposal. Disposal documents will be sent to you as part of the closure summary.Range intends to remediate this release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1)".The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan and the SDS for the spilled material were on site. The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan was not observed (Photos 1, 2). It was unclear if the SDS was on site before and during the spill incident.I observed two unlabeled roll-offs on site (Photos 3, 4). I recommend labeling the roll-offs.The impacted area appeared to have been excavated and remediated. The area appeared to be approximately 25 x 20 feet in size (Photos 5-10).The source of the spilled material originated within the tan container, which was placed on secondary containment. The labeling of the container did not match the SDS. I observed an absorbent pad within the containment (Photos 11-14).An additional container was within the impacted area. The labeling of this container did not appear to be the same as the tan container (spill origin). This container appeared to be double walled and does not require secondary containment (Photos 15, 16).Violations of 78a54 and SWMA 301 are being issued for the spill.

Comments: I stopped to do a follow up inspection in relation to the spill of a lube oil that occurred on 3/2/21 at this McCullough well site. I arrived on site with Brady Johnson (DEP) and we met Brett Bunker (Hilcorp Energy). He filled us in on the clean up details. Basically, they have moved the compressor and excavated most of the impacted material and are just dealing with some "hot spot" areas. The spill hit hard pan under the gravel and confined the oil to mainly only traveling 8" to 12" vertically. The impacted material was in 4 roll off containers and they will have more as the contractor (ACV Enviro) is continuing to remove some more contaminated material. Brett feels the clean up work should be done by the end of today.

properties.content:

Violation ID: 987747
Permit API: 015-23717
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/08/2023
Comments: On 3/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine/complete inspection at the Chesapeake Floydie well site. It was 32 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. I did not see a Chesapeake site leader during the inspection.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by six infiltration berms that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.There are six existing wells that were being set up for production and four new wells that were being set up for flowback. Well permit numbers were posted at the entrance to the access road. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. There were twelve frac tanks on site that were being staged in secondary containment during the inspection.There were water puddles scattered across the pad surface that were field tested for conductivity with the following results: A 30' x 10' water puddle about midway on the southeast side of the pad field tested at 7.06 mS conductance. A 20' x 60' water/mud puddle east of the wellheads field tested at as high as 13.01 mS conductance. I collected sample number 9551-046 from this water puddle. A 20' x 30' water/mud puddle near the southern end of the southeast side field tested at 5.40 mS conductance. A 20' x 20' water puddle near the south corner of the pad field tested at 2.02 mS conductance. Water puddles on other areas of the pad field tested at less than 1.0 mS conductance. These areas of elevated conductance fluid were under frac secondary containment during recent completion activities. They are further north of the area sampled in inspection #3492400 with 11.93 mS conductance fluids where sample 9551-039 was collected from. They are south of the 4.90 mS conductance fluids where sample 9551-040 was collected from.Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 for the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.The DEP recommends removing the debris from the rock channel between the cut slope and the site containment berm.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3492400 for elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface in two locations.I left the site at 1500 hours.

Violation ID: 8196389

Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/29/2024
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Blackhill Energy's Nichols A (1H) well site located in Smithfield Township, Bradford County on 7/29/2024 at 1120 hours. The weather was 77 degrees F with mostly clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a discovered release reported by the operator. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #382564 is tied to this release within CTS.On 7/29/2024 at ~0815 hours, Blackhill Energy discovered a produced water release to the pad surface at their Nichols (A) well site. The release appeared to come from a water truck after or during recovering water from the produced water tank onsite. Blackhill Energy is unsure of the total amount of the release. Moody and Associates, Fenton Transport/Trucking, and Blackhill Energy representatives were all present during my visit. During my inspection, the overview of the release area was observed. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 961506
Permit API: 081-21878
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/11/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow-up after on 6/24/2022, the operator reported a release of 140 barrels of produced fluid to the secondary containment, some of which then overflowed the secondary containment and flowed onto the pad surface. I first inspected Pad B. I met with company man Walt Arnold upon arriving on location. I saw a piece of discarded secondary containment that was sitting on the rig mats for the sandboxes near the pad entrance. Some fluid was dripping off of the containment and onto the rig mats. I asked the company man if there was secondary containment beneath the rig mats and he said no. I recommended to him that the discarded containment be placed on secondary containment until it could be thrown away. He said that he would have someone put it on secondary containment right away. Before I left the pad, the discarded containment was on its own secondary containment. Fluid with a electrical conductivity (EC) of >19.99 mS/cm as measured by the Oakton conductivity meter is present on the secondary containment for the blender. The Department recommends vacuuming out the containment. Fluid with an EC of between 1.6 to 2.3 mS/cm was observed on the pad surface near the northeast corner of the pad where some secondary containment was removed from the pad surface. The Department recommends scraping up the fluid in this area of the pad. Along the east side of the pad, at the southeast corner of the secondary containment for the produced water tanks, I observed staining and dampness on the pad surface. I also observed the dampness beneath the secondary containment berm as well. The fluid beneath the berm had an EC of >19.99 mS/cm as measured by the Oakton conductivity meter. The fluid present inside the containment also had an EC of >19.99 mS/cm. I also got the same reading when I pressed the meter probes into the mud on the pad surface. The visibly impacted area adjacent to the secondary containment was approximately 5 square feet in total. The surface area impacted beneath the secondary containment is unknown. When the berm of the secondary containment was lifted by EQT personnel, the pad surface beneath the containment appeared damp. I took a soil sample from the pad surface adjacent to the containment berm and slightly beneath the berm. There was not enough fluid on the pad surface to take a water sample. The sample is number 0718-196 which will be sent to the state laboratory to be analyzed for SAC 530 + Li and Br. Violations pending sample results.I also met with Rick Hall of EQT during this inspection and I showed him the area where I found the dampness, staining, and fluid at the corner of the produced water secondary containment. Violations remain outstanding for the release on 6/24/2022.

Violation ID: 948073
Permit API: 083-49666
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report of an oil and gas leak in the vicinity of Chappel Fork near the road crossing of RT 321 (CTS #362745). At the time of the report to DEP, I spoke to the complainant and determined the location to begin searching. I contacted Pennhills Resources as they have wells in the immediate vicinity, and we agreed to meet on site to look. After beginning at Rt 321 we headed east until we found some oil collected in a low spot. It appears as though a line has burst with some gas pressure on the line, causing oil and gas to bubble to the surface. The oil then flowed south and into a low swale, where the majority of it collected. Some crude then flowed through into a channel formed by the collection of two spring runs, and toward the main branch of Chappel Fork. Oil was collecting behind ice pockets and in between leaves and dead vegetation for approximately 200 feet. A small amount of sheen was noted in Chappel Fork, but no free product. Approximately 15-20 barrels of oil was emitted from the line in total. Another small area nearer to the creek when following the line was noted to contain some basic sediment and paraffin at the surface and under a hemlock tree; it is uncertain if this is another leak site or simply product following the line. Pennhills immediately moved to contain the spill with booms in the back channel, and then brought a mini excavator to site to dig up the line and slow the leak. The 2" line was uncovered and a band placed on the line, which was broken on the bottom. It was determined that the old access past well 9A could be used to mobilize equipment and some brush was removed to make for better access. A vac truck was brought to site to collect any free product available, which was able to get a large amount on the first load. It was determined the evening of 3/15 that the line belonged to Pennhills, who will be continuing to clean up the oil and soil until clean. The operator built two underflow dams to contain any free product flowing down the channel with melting ice starting to give way. Followup inspection will be performed as necessary.

At the time of the report to DEP, I spoke to the complainant and determined the location to begin searching. I contacted Pennhills Resources as they have wells in the immediate vicinity, and we agreed to meet on site to look. After beginning at Rt 321 we headed east until we found some oil collected in a low spot. It appears as though a line has burst with some gas pressure on the line, causing oil and gas to bubble to the surface. The oil then flowed south and into a low swale, where the majority of it collected. Some crude then flowed through into a channel formed by the collection of two spring runs, and toward the main branch of Chappel Fork. Oil was collecting behind ice pockets and in between leaves and dead vegetation for approximately 200 feet. A small amount of sheen was noted in Chappel Fork, but no free product. Approximately 15-20 barrels of oil was emitted from the line in total. Another small area nearer to the creek when following the line was noted to contain some basic sediment and paraffin at the surface and under a hemlock tree; it is uncertain if this is another leak site or simply product following the line. Pennhills immediately moved to contain the spill with booms in the back channel, and then brought a mini excavator to site to dig up the line and slow the leak. The 2" line was uncovered and a band placed on the line, which was broken on the bottom. It was determined that the old access past well 9A could be used to mobilize equipment and some brush was removed to make for better access. A vac truck was brought to site to collect any free product available, which was able to get a large amount on the first load. It was determined the evening of 3/15 that the line belonged to Pennhills, who will be continuing to clean up the oil and soil until clean. The operator built two underflow dams to contain any free product flowing down the channel with melting ice starting to give way. Followup inspection will be performed as necessary.

Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

Violation ID: 922659
Permit API: 053-27124
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/08/2021
Comments: Responded to a call from Minard Run to Scott Motter ( Dep representative) in regards that there had been a crude oil spill at one of there tank batteries in Forest County, Howe Township PA. Upon arriving on location I met with Minard Run Representative Gary Davis and USFS Mike Lewis. They gave a brief run down of the incident and work that had been completed to stop the flow of Crude Oil. There was a failure at well 053-27124. A valve broke which was connected to a steel line on the exit side of the check valve, which is going to tank battery. Minard Run is on site. A new valve was installed. Booms and pads were in place at the time of my arrival. They are Currently digging diversion ditches and a siphon dam. Crude product left the well site, traveled the road ditch, and went through a culvert. At that point some of the product went into a fresh water pond and some oil diverted around the pond into a wet land and then into a wooded area. Once it entered the wooded area the product penetrated the large rock structure area and flowed underground to the fresh water tributary. Pictures show where Minard Run placed booms to attempt to stop the flow down stream. The flow is carrying some product further down stream, in which they have more booms in place. It was approx estimate of 2 to 3 barrels of crude leaked. Minard Run was going to try to get a volume of the gathering lines to help identify the volume. It was suggested to add additional booms down stream and continue with the current clean up process. In light of future rains tonight it was suggested to leave booms in-place and remove pads to prevent them being pushed down stream. Minard Run did an excellent job responding and attempting to clean up the oil in the early stages of the incident. This will be forwarded to WQS for follow up.

At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the plugged well site to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/15/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Brokenstraw Township, Warren county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/15/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8278407
Permit API: 123-45905
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Brokenstraw Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/15/2026
Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Conklin Lease tank battery. Mature trees at the southwest corner of the secondary containment area are either heavily stressed or dead. A brine tank is buried within the secondary containment area. PVC lines connect the drain valves of the stock tanks in containment to cutout holes in the surface of the brine tank. Evidence of previous fluid releases in the containment area are visible via crude oil staining and sawdust sprinkled over the oil-stained areas. It appears that the PVC lines connected to the two stock tanks in the southernmost end of the containment area have been the most heavily used. At the time of this inspection, the PVC lines are placed inside the cutout holes of the brine tank. However, oil-staining, visible wetness, and sawdust sprinkled around these cutout holes indicate that at one time fluid was allowed to run over the surface of the brine tank and onto the ground within the secondary containment area. Elevated specific conductance in soils in excess of 3,000 uS/cm was observed beneath both of the aforementioned PVC lines.A pool of fluid was present in the southernmost end of the containment area, in what appeared to be a sump. At the time of this inspection, the fluid was observed to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 4,000 uS/cm. Soils at the bottom of the sump also had elevated specific conductance which measured in excess of 11,000 uS/cm. The floor of the secondary containment area above the sump was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 2,000 uS/cm. A drainage swale is located approximately 30 feet west of the secondary containment area wall. Upslope soil conductivity readings in the swale were observed at 96 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance in excess of 4,000 uS/cm was observed in soils within the swale directly across from the tank battery. Crude oil staining was also observed in the swale near the tank battery. The swale transitions to an UNT to Irvine Run with defined bed and banks downslope of the tank battery. The water flowing in the UNT was found to have elevated specific conductance exceeding 13,000 uS/cm. Elevated specific conductance of water was observed throughout the stream at the time of this inspection. The specific conductance of water in the stream was observed to drop below 1,000 uS/cm after two confluences with apparently unaffected sources of fresh water at a point approximately 200 feet north of a culvert and the lease road which crosses the UNT. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with brine disposal receipts for the Conklin lease.

Report Details
Operator: Diversified Oil & Gas Llc

Violation Date: 2019-12-23
Violation Code: 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
Violation ID: 872384
Permit API: 059-24428
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-23
Comments: On 12/19/19 a malfunction with the GPU occurred, causing the vessel to explode. On 12/20/19 OGI Joel Keller conducted inspection 2974755 and noted soil staining and a damp appearance. OGI Keller requested a follow up inspection be conducted by a WQS. On 12/23/19 at approximately 0800 I conducted a follow up inspection. The temperature was well below freezing at the time of inspection. Upon arriving at the explosion location I observed water on the access road that was not frozen, despite the freezing temperature. A soil conductivity probe was utilized and a reading od 12.02mS was observed (see photograph). Additional elevated soil conductivity readings were observed throughout the access road and on the east side of the access road. Trees and shrubs on the east side of the access road appeared wet. The liquid was not frozen and appeared to be brine, as further demonstrated by elevated soil conductivity readings in the area. No other trees or shrubs appeared wet, except for those east of the GPU location where elevated soil conductivity was observed. Additional elevated soil conductivity readings were observed further North toward the well head on the east side of the access road (see photographs). Elevated soil conductivity readings were also observed adjacent to brine tank 2. The highest reading observed was 12.83mS. Both brine tanks were severely corroded and brine tank 2 exhibited a large hole (see photographs). Brine tank 1 exhibited several smaller holes that appeared to have occurred due to shrapnel from the GPU explosion. The gravel in the former GPU location appeared to be stained, but the soil conductivity was not elevated. The Department recommends the visually impacted material is removed. Soil sample 3402-076 was collected from an area exhibiting elevated soil conductivity. Soil sample 3402-077 was collected from an area on the northwest portion of the site in an area that appeared to be unimpaired with low notably lower soil conductivity (see photographs). The Department recommends the spill is addressed consistent with the Act 2 process.

Comments: On January 31, 2025 the Department conducted an Incident inspection of the PF Eisaman South 43 well pad located in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County in response to a spill that reportedly occurred on Monday, January 27, 2025. Accompanying on today's inspection is CNX representative Jessie Valentine. Comments: On 1/23/23 CHK reported a release of 42 gallons of produced water onto the pad surface. The release occurred around 11:00 on 1/23/23 when a produced water tank dump valve stuck open. It was estimated that the affected area was about 20' x 20'. The produced water tank was located on the northern side of the pad near the access road. At the time of inspection, the impacted area was revised to approximately 60' x 70' oriented north-south by east-west. The excavated area was approximately 10" - 12" deep. The excavation was being guided by conductivity measurements performed by Creston. The produced water tank will need to be moved in order to excavate the impacted area near the base and under the tank. The full depth of the excavation can not be determined until the tank is cleaned and moved, likely tomorrow 1/25/23.Conductivity measurements were taken around the the perimeter of the excavation. The measurements ranged from 0.02 to 0.390 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). A roadside ditch running along the access road and leading to an infiltration basin below the produced water tank was also inspected and screened. The site was snow-covered and no visual evidence of runoff was noted. Soil conductivity readings were below 0.20 mS/cm.The result of the inspection is Violations Noted and Act 2 remediation will be pursued.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 5/06/2026
Comments: On 5/06/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection in response to a complaint (CTS-397312) at the Clara Jacques 1 well plugging site in Wharton Township, Fayette County. This inspection also follows-up to IR 4186065, where violations were issued against severe tire rutting observed in the access road.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site after in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216; after completion of plugging operations.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance along Five Forks Road (photos 1 and 2). An additional RCE is installed where the access road meets the well site, in accordance with the E and S plan drawing. The RCE adjacent to the well plugging site is laden with sediment (photos 15 and 22). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed on site in the locations shown on E and S plan drawing (photos 9, 12, 17, 19, and 20). Significant tire rutting remains throughout the access road. Due to the soft and damp soil conditions that appear to exist on site, the Department recommended in IR 4186065 that the operator consider additional E and S control measures as necessary, to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring on site. Well plugging equipment was observed on site, however plugging operations do not appear to be occurring at the time of inspection. A puddle with swirly rainbow sheen was observed adjacent to well plugging rig. This swirly rainbow sheen remained intact when disturbed, which is a known indicator of a petroleum-based release.The Department identified an access road cross-culvert at the time of IR 4186065 (photo 23). No loose sediment was observed in the cross-culvert during this inspection. However, the Department recommended in IR 4186065 that the operator take necessary measures to ensure that the cross-culvert is protected from sedimentation.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4186065 shall remain outstanding. Additional violations shall be issued for failure to adequately protect the cross-culvert shown in Photo 14 and for failure maintain the RCE adjacent to the well plugging site. Additional volations may be forthcoming against the swirly rainbow sheen released adjacent to the well plugging rig.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Seneca Resource's Peffer Strong 483 well site located in Sullivan Township, Tioga County on 9/6/2022 at 1120 hours. The weather was 67 degrees with cloudy skies. Rain fell onsite within the past 24 hours. During today's inspection, a section of the secondary containment structure located in the center of the pad was overtopping with fluid. A sheen was observed atop the fluid that was observed overtopping the secondary containment wall. Sample 0983-345 was collected from the fluid located just outside of the overtopping containment wall (photo #5). Fluids held in the center of the pad overtopping the containment that was field measured ranged from 320 to 430us/cm. 25 Pa. Code 78a.64a.(e) states "Operator failed to remove stormwater as soon as possible and prior to the capacity of secondary containment being reduced by 10% or more." Areas where elevated conductivity pad material and fluid were discovered in a 6/23/2022 inspection report were reevaluated today. Pooled fluids located near the entrance were now field measured at a range of 480 to 840us/cm. Elevated conductivity pad material located in front of the produced water tanks' offload area was now field measured at a range of 0.2 to 0.3mS/cm. The area located just southeast of the Gas Processing Units (GPUs) secondary containment (photo #6) where elevated conductivity pad material was discovered on 6/23/2022 is now retaining fluid that was field measured at ~3.72mS/cm. Sample 0983-344 was collected from this fluid. Just east of this area, a rock-lined stormwater channel was retaining fluid that was field measured at ~2.30mS/cm today. Sample 0983-343 was collected from the rock-lined channel (photo #8). Based on the findings of today's inspection, violations of the following cited against API #117-22110 cited on 7/7/2022 remain outstanding at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.30135 P.S. 691.402(b)In addition, a violation of the following is also cited against API #117-22110 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.64a(e)Additional violations are pending, awaiting sample results 0983-343, 344, and 345. I departed the site at 1255 hours.
